title: Musicians still in Jackson, Hattiesburg and Bogalusa
summary: He names the Pomler brothers, Joe White and other players in Mississippi and Louisiana towns.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yeah, well I was going to speak about some musicians. Still around that way, down around New Orleans, Jackson, Mississippi there. They got Doc Pomler, he's a mighty good trumpet player. He's in Jackson still. Jackson. His brother, he's a good bass, tuba player. Edmund Pomler, his name, we call him Luke. His name's Edmund Pomler. Also, they got one of the world's greatest show drummers around there, Joe White.
So well, yes, I've heard of him. Well, he's in Jackson. He's in Jackson.
I think he's still there. He played New Orleans too, didn't he?
Oh yeah, he played all around.
I guess most of those fellows. We'll have to get up to Jackson sometime. Yeah, that's right. Interview those people.
So, Luke, Edmund Pomler has a cafe there on Oakland and Mill Street.
I thought at first it said Palmer maybe. Pomler. Pomler. Well, maybe we can get up there and see those fellows and talk to them too and interview them later. That's right.
Do you remember anybody else in Hattiesburg that might be there? Or Bogalusa?
Well, I think they all did. Or Bogalusa. They died out there. Emile Thomas, he were there, but he passed here not so awfully long ago.

Well, most of those who have left, they had Sabadeo Arty. He was a pretty good piano player, but I think he lived at, past Christian now. He moved over from Bogalusa. Martin Davis, he was a, Martin Davis, he was a pretty good piano player. He lived in Hattiesburg. So I think they mostly, some in California.
